title: Different types of families (Year 1 lesson)
desc: A short lesson on how families can be made up in many different ways, with materials you can download.
how: Use after the family survey; ask how families in your building or village differ.

title: No two families are the same (Key Stage 2 lesson)
desc: An older-child lesson asking whether there is such a thing as a perfect family, with downloadable materials.
how: Good with the 'Families in 50 years' sheet for Classes 4–5.

title: Family changes (Key Stage 2 lesson)
desc: A lesson about how families change over time, from the unit 'Do all families look the same?'.

title: Harvest festival around the world
desc: A Year 2 lesson on how people in different places celebrate the harvest, from a unit on festivals that celebrate the natural world.
how: Pair with Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi or Bihu: why do so many festivals fall at harvest time?

title: The celebration of Holi
desc: A Year 2 lesson on Holi as a festival connected with the natural world and the season.

title: The festival of trees
desc: A Year 2 lesson on a festival that celebrates trees, from the unit on festivals and the natural world.
how: Ask: which Indian festivals honour trees or plants (Vat Purnima, Tulsi Vivah)?

title: Festival fun
desc: A lesson about different festivals and how people celebrate them, ending with making a celebration card.

title: Who Ate All That Up?
desc: A Creative Commons picture book by Sejal Mehta, illustrated by Rohan Chakravarty, about why nothing goes to waste in a forest: from leftover food to elephant dung, every animal down to the dung beetle helps clean up.
how: Read it before the waste sheets and ask: is there an 'away' to throw things to in a forest? In a city?

title: Up World, Down World
source: Pratham Books StoryWeaver (via Free Kids Books)
desc: A Creative Commons story set in a forest canopy, about the many creatures living high in the trees and low on the ground, and friendship between them.

title: Food-science projects for Grade 3: health
desc: A list of seven kitchen science projects for about age 8–9 about food and health, each with steps and background.
how: Pick one that uses things in an Indian kitchen.
